title: Initial `avg_line_bytes = file_size / max(n_preview, 1)` is effectively dead and `max(n_preview, 1)` is redundant inside `if n_preview > 0`
description: Inside `if n_preview > 0`, the first assignment `avg_line_bytes = file_size / max(n_preview, 1)` (line 114) is immediately overwritten by `avg_line_bytes = sample_bytes / n_preview` whenever `sample_bytes > 0` (line 121). `sample_bytes = sum(len(line)+1 for line in preview_df.write_ndjson().splitlines())` is > 0 for any non-empty preview (even a row serialising to `{}` contributes `len('{}')+1 = 3`), so for every reachable input with `n_preview > 0` the initial value is discarded. The `max(n_preview, 1)` guard is also redundant because the enclosing `if n_preview > 0` already guarantees `n_preview >= 1`. The block can be reduced to computing `sample_bytes`, then `avg_line_bytes = sample_bytes / n_preview` (with sample_bytes guaranteed positive), removing the dead initial assignment and the redundant `max`.
evidence: Line 114 sets avg_line_bytes; lines 120-121 overwrite it under `if sample_bytes > 0`. write_ndjson of a non-empty frame always yields >0 bytes, making the `if sample_bytes > 0` always true and the line-114 value dead. `max(n_preview, 1)` is inside `if n_preview > 0` (line 113).
behavior_preservation: Identical for all reachable inputs: whenever n_preview>0 the preview is non-empty so sample_bytes>0 and the estimator already uses sample_bytes/n_preview; the removed branch only ever executed in the impossible 'non-empty preview serialises to 0 bytes' case.
